# Channel-1 ctx_reduce compliance grace

## Finding

Channel 1 previously treated any reclaimable-tail collapse as a cycle reset. A successful `ctx_reduce` therefore cleared the persisted level and watermark, so the first post-drop tool result looked like a new band crossing and could receive another full imperative reminder. The real-user-turn dampener only selected sticky wording; after its short window expired, a same-band cadence fire could return to full wording.

The queued-drop accounting was already correct: queued tags remain in total rendered mass T but are excluded from actionable mass U. The missing constraint was when compliance grace captured its baseline. Capturing pre-drop U would make the queued-drop subtraction look like immediate regrowth and void the grace interval.

## Fix

The OpenCode and Pi legs now store grace inside the existing `session_meta.last_nudge_level` JSON value; no database column was added. A `ctx_reduce` call first records a pending grace state and preserves the observed band. The next trustworthy tail walk captures U only after queued drops have been excluded. Invalidated measurements leave grace pending rather than capturing stale U.

The Rust leg mirrors the same state in the existing serialized tail-hygiene baseline inside module metadata. A pass applying agent drops captures the post-exclusion U value while preserving the frozen measurement baseline and rendered bytes.

All three legs now apply these rules:

- Channel 1 stays quiet until U grows by `max(25k, 0.08 × T)` from post-drop U, or the band rises above the pre-reduce band.
- An upward transition into gentle, firm, or urgent renders full copy once. Same-band cadence fires use only the existing calm sticky copy.
- Sticky fires require five real user turns since the previous Channel-1 emission. Successive tool results in one turn cannot repeat full copy.
- Urgent escalation breaks grace. Channel 2 evaluates independently of Channel-1 grace, and emergency paths are unchanged.
- The phrase `a ctx_reduce pass is due` remains confined to first-crossing urgent copy. Sticky copy and all rendered bands remain denominator-free.

## Regression and parity coverage

The OpenCode hook, shared TypeScript decision function, Pi tool-result handler, and Rust decision tests pin the compliance sequence: first nudge, `ctx_reduce`, immediate post-drop output, sub-delta regrowth, and exact-delta re-fire. Separate arms cover upward escalation, Channel-2 independence, same-band wording, five-turn cadence, pure tool-stream repeats, and byte-identical replay while grace is active.

`bun crates/mc-module/gen/gen-nudge-hygiene-golden.ts` regenerated the 14-case differential corpus. The generated bytes remained stable, and the Rust consumer plus Pi parity tests byte-match the TypeScript reference.

## Executed mutation evidence

Each deliberate source mutation used the exact `NON-VACUITY BREAK` marker and was restored immediately:

- Disabling the shared TypeScript grace predicate made the focused plugin run fail at `ctx-reduce-nudge.test.ts:204` (the immediate decision fired) and `hook-handlers.test.ts:788` (the sub-delta output gained a sticky reminder). The Pi twin failed at `ctx-reduce-nudge-pi.test.ts:380` for the same sub-delta re-fire.
- Disabling Rust `post_reduce_grace_holds` made `post_reduce_grace_uses_post_drop_u_and_breaks_on_escalation` fail at `transform.rs:10043` because the immediate decision fired.

The mutations were restored and all focused mutation targets passed. No `NON-VACUITY BREAK` marker remains in changed source or tests.
